### [1:35–3:15] STEP 1 — BUILD THE INVOICE ZAP  (send it automatically)
**NARRATION:** "Step one: the invoice sends itself. In Zapier, every automation is called a Zap,
and a Zap is just two halves — a trigger and an action. The trigger is *when* it runs. The action
is *what* it does. So: log into Zapier, click Create, and pick your trigger — something like 'a new
row is added to my jobs spreadsheet,' or 'a deal is marked Won.' Then pick your action — 'create
and send an invoice' in whatever you use, QuickBooks, Stripe, PayPal, Xero. Map the fields once —
customer name here, amount here — and flip it on. Done."
**[VISUAL]:** Screen-record in Zapier: **Create → Trigger (Google Sheets, 'New row') → Action
(invoicing app, 'Send invoice') → map name + amount → toggle ON.**
**[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "An invoice should send the moment the work's done — not three days
later when you finally remember."

### [3:15–4:45] STEP 2 — ADD THE PAYMENT CHASE  (reminders on autopilot)
**NARRATION:** "Step two: the invoice chases itself. This is the one that actually gets you paid.
Build a second Zap that triggers when the invoice is due. Add a Delay step — say, seven days. Then
add a Filter — 'only keep going if this invoice is still unpaid.' Then the action: send a friendly
reminder email. Want a firmer nudge a week later? Add another delay and a second message. Now late
payments get chased without you ever being the bad guy."
**[VISUAL]:** Zapier path builds on screen: **Invoice due → Delay 7 days → Filter 'Unpaid?' →
Send reminder email.** Show a short, polite reminder draft.
**[PATTERN INTERRUPT]:** Text slam — **"Most late payments aren't refusals. They're people who
forgot. A polite automatic nudge gets you paid without you playing bad cop."**

**[VISUAL]:** Subscribe animation + Ep 11 thumbnail peeks in.

### [5:30–7:00] STEP 3 — AUTO-FILE RECEIPTS & DATA ENTRY  (the AI part)
**NARRATION:** "Step three: receipts file themselves, and this is where the AI really earns its
keep. Build a Zap that triggers on a new email with a receipt — or a new file in a 'Receipts'
folder. Then add an AI step. Zapier has one built in, and it runs on models like Google Gemini.
Point it at the receipt and tell it, in plain English: pull out the vendor, the date, the amount,
and the category. It reads the receipt like a person would, then hands those details to the next
action — add a row to your bookkeeping sheet, and save the file to the right Drive folder.
That's your data entry, gone."
**[VISUAL]:** Flow on screen: **Email receipt → AI step reads it (vendor · date · amount ·
category) → New row in sheet + file saved to Drive folder.**
**[TAKEAWAY on screen]:** "Data entry is just moving information from one box to another — the
exact job software was born to do."

### [7:00–8:20] STEP 4 — THE PAYBACK MATH  (is it worth it?)
**NARRATION:** "Step four: the number I promised. Add up the hours admin steals from you each
week. For most owners, invoicing and admin runs about four hours. Four hours a week, times fifty
working weeks, is two hundred hours a year — that's five full work-weeks. Now put your own hourly
rate on those hours. Even at modest numbers, you're looking at thousands of dollars and more than
a month of work, handed back to you. And remember the stat: two-thirds of businesses already save
five hundred to two thousand a month with AI — admin is a big slice of that. Your cost to build
the 3-Zap Stack? One afternoon, and pennies a month to run."
**[VISUAL]:** Formula fills in on screen: **hours/week × 50 weeks × your rate = your payback.**
Then **4 × 50 = 200 hrs/yr.**
